title: 기분 말하기: 오늘 기분이 어때요?
objective: By the end, you can say how you feel in short polite sentences ending in -아요/-어요, like 피곤해요 or 기뻐요, and answer the question "기분이 어때요?"
summary: Learn ten basic Korean words for talking about how you feel, such as glad, sad, tired, angry and happy.

task.title: Talk about your feelings
task.line: Read each short situation, then choose, write or order the Korean words that show the feeling.

words.meaning: feeling, mood (how you feel right now)
to be glad, to feel happy about something good (기뻐요)
words.exampleMeaning: I passed the exam. I'm so glad.
This song is a little sad.
I went to bed late last night, so I'm tired.

words.meaning: to get angry, to be upset (화나요; also 화가 나요)
to be happy (a warm, lasting feeling) (행복해요)
to be bored, to have nothing to do (심심해요)
words.exampleMeaning: I have nothing to do this weekend. I'm bored.

words.meaning: to be okay, to be fine (괜찮아요)
words.exampleMeaning: A: Are you tired? B: No, I'm fine.

exercises: Choose the word that fits: ① 생일 선물을 받았어요. (기뻐요 / 슬퍼요) ② 친한 친구가 고향으로 돌아가요. (슬퍼요 / 심심해요) ③ 열 시간 동안 일했어요. (행복해요 / 피곤해요)
Write the -아요/-어요 form of the word in brackets: ① 텔레비전도 없고 친구도 없어요. 너무 ____. (심심하다) ② 이 만화는 정말 재미있어요. 그래서 계속 ____. (웃다)
Fill in the blank with 화나요, 울어요 or 괜찮아요: ① 친구가 약속을 또 잊었어요. 저는 너무 ____. ② 영화가 너무 슬퍼요. 그래서 저는 ____. ③ A: 많이 아파요? B: 아니요, ____.
Answer in Korean with 행복하다: 주말에 가족을 만나요. 기분이 어때요?
Put the words in order to make a sentence: 기뻐요 / 저는 / 정말
answers: ① 기뻐요 ② 슬퍼요 ③ 피곤해요
① 화나요 (화가 나요) ② 울어요 ③ 괜찮아요
